note: A sea backdrop: the primary's three places seated on the ocean datum, the hall and the annex wing with their walk planes one course above the sea (frame at 60, floor at 63) and the long hall's floor at 63 over a ground one course under it. It is a different world for the same campaign and cannot coexist with `void`. It builds from the SHORE set: the same hall and the same annex tiles lifted onto two courses of plinth, with a tide pool cut into the floor course so each piece's top water block lands on the sea plane and `waterline_y` can say so — the annex wing's program imports its tiles' waterline with their anchors. It is the only point of this domain where the sea proofs have anything to look at: `validation/fluid-escape.json` (`DW0318`), `validation/sea-seepage.json` (`DW0851`), and the `DW0344` waterline binding, which a bound shore's frame is held to.
